articles.title: Ultrasound offers a scalable path to tactile intelligence for physical AI
articles.summary: The article argues that tactile sensing is a key bottleneck for physical AI systems such as humanoid hands, dexterous grippers, logistics robots, service robots, and industrial systems. UltraSense says protected sub-surface ultrasound sensing could scale better than surface-coupled electronic skin by reducing exposure to abrasion, compression, contamination, drift, and recalibration burden. Ultrasound can potentially support multi-parameter touch data, including contact, force distribution, shear, slip, and material interaction.
articles.advisor_relevance: This matters because manipulation remains a major constraint for real-world robotics adoption, and durable tactile sensing could be an enabling component for humanoids, grippers, logistics automation, service robots, and industrial systems. The article highlights a potential shift from exposed electronic-skin approaches toward protected sensing architectures, which may be relevant for identifying component-level beneficiaries as physical AI moves toward commercial deployment. However, the piece is primarily technical and does not provide customer deployments, revenue traction, financing, or market sizing.
